review_method.normative_instructions: CLAUDE.md and applicable audit workflow read fully.
review_method.rendering: Every receipt-listed tile was individually opened using tools.view_image at original resolution; per-tile view attestations and actual SHA256 values are recorded.
review_method.source_snapshot_html: Every frozen title and complete ItemBody was checked against the matching current source, frozen snapshot, receipt, and local HTML; hashes are recorded per item.
review_method.boundary: Local-only inspection. No live website/network, item/library/application edits, or publication-status changes.

findings.rationale: The example's main computation is organized around the positively oriented boundary of the unit square: four directed edges, outward normals, and separate flux contributions 0, 1, 1/2, 0. A compact diagram could pair each edge orientation and outward normal with its contribution and clarify the boundary-versus-interior comparison. This is a substantive teaching candidate, not a rendering defect.

concrete_maps_and_relations.field_and_flux: F(x,y)=(x^2,xy); outward normal flux form is (-F_y) dx + F_x dy; directed edge contributions are 0, 1, 1/2, 0 and sum to 3/2.

findings.rationale: The example is built around a specific geometric path and its orientation: the right half of the unit circle from (0,-1) to (0,1). A small diagram can locate the arc, endpoints, and direction while distinguishing the scalar ds integral's orientation independence. This is a substantive teaching candidate, not a rendering defect.

concrete_maps_and_relations.curve: gamma(t)=(cos t,sin t), -pi/2 <= t <= pi/2; right unit semicircle from bottom to top.
concrete_maps_and_relations.value_and_orientation: The scalar arc-length integral is integral_gamma x ds=2 and remains 2 under path reversal.

findings.rationale: The counterexample depends on a distinctive triangulation: m horizontal bands on a cylinder with n vertices per ring and successive rings shifted by pi/n. The mesh tends to zero under m=n^3 while the area diverges. A cylinder-and-unwrapped-strip diagram would make the staggered rings, triangular faces, and competing mesh/area limits far clearer. This is a high-value candidate, not a rendering defect.

concrete_maps_and_relations.surface: Cylinder of radius r>0 and height H>0; m equal horizontal bands and n vertices per ring.
concrete_maps_and_relations.staggering: Successive rings differ in angular phase by pi/n; each band has 2n congruent inscribed triangles.
concrete_maps_and_relations.limit_sequence: Set m=n^3: maximum edge length tends to zero, while A_{m,n}=2rn sin(pi/n) sqrt(H^2+m^2 r^2(1-cos(pi/n))^2) tends to +infinity.

findings.rationale: The counterexample contrasts a smooth double-cone level set with a regular surface away from its apex and a rank-zero derivative at the apex. A diagram showing the two nappes, apex, and the listed independent cone rays makes the failure of a single tangent plane at the apex immediate. This is a substantive candidate, not a rendering defect.

concrete_maps_and_relations.map: F:R^3->R, F(x,y,z)=x^2+y^2-z^2; zero level is x^2+y^2=z^2.
concrete_maps_and_relations.rank: DF(x,y,z)=(2x,2y,-2z), hence rank 0 at (0,0,0) and rank 1 at every other point of the cone.
concrete_maps_and_relations.rays: The cone contains directions (1,0,1), (1,0,-1), and (0,1,1), which span R^3 and therefore are not all contained in a two-dimensional tangent plane.
